title: Hey Mom…
subtitle: Recipes and stories from 28 years of feeding the people I love.
author: Missy
intro:
My name is Missy Delaria, and I learned to cook on the banks of the Niagara River. I grew up in Grand Island, a suburb just outside Buffalo, New York, in a house that looked across the water to Canada. We were a typical family of four — my mother stayed home, my father worked, and my sister was six and a half years older than me, off doing her own things. Truthfully, my mom and grandmother were not big cooks. I treasure the couple of their recipes I still make today, but the kitchen was mostly mine to figure out. I really learned to cook from three places: from Suzie — Mrs. Wiles, a housekeeper in our neighborhood — who gave me my foundation and the real how-to of it; a little bit from my mom; and a great deal from myself, by experimenting, trying things, and simply having the drive and the desire to make good food for the people I love.

Years later, I met my husband in 1989, when we were college sweethearts. We married in 1995 in Wayzata, Minnesota, bought a wonderful little house in Deep Haven, and began building a life of our own. In August of 1997 we welcomed our first child, Kendall, and in September of 1999 we completed our family with our twins, Stockton and Larkin — and just like that, we were a family of five. When the children arrived, we had a decision to make: would I keep working, or stay home? We chose for me to stay home, and I have been devoted to that choice ever since.

For twenty-eight years, my work has been raising our children and feeding our family — putting nutritious, wonderful-tasting, fun food on the table every single day. Food became the center of our home: the everyday dinners, the lunches and after-school snacks, the holidays, the parties, and all the friends and family who gathered around our table along the way. This book is everything I learned in those years, from the technique Suzie first taught me to the dishes my own kids grew up on. More than anything, it's an invitation. I want to welcome you into my years of experience at the stove — and I hope, in some small way, it helps with yours.
